news.abstract: India and Sri Lanka have promised to spare no expense to help tens of thousands whose lives were overturned in tsunami disaster; Sri Lanka is welcoming international aid, but India says it needs no outside help; newly wealthy, in region with history of natural calamity but uneven civic response, have played new role, raising money and delivering aid where wealthy Western countries once did; efforts have frequently been poorly focused, uncoordinated and blunted in some cases by distrust among government officials; situation in Nagappattinam, India, port town where 2,000 people died, noted; map; photos (M)
news.title: As Officials Falter, the New Rich Roll in to Help

news.abstract: Sudan government signs preliminary peace accord with Sudan People's Liberation Army that could end one of Africa's longest-running civil wars, even as conflict in Darfur continues; southern rebels took up arms in 1983, saying oil revenue was benefiting only north; rebel leader John Garang will become one of Pres Omar Hassan Ahmad al-Bashir's vice presidents under agreement; photos (M)
news.title: Sudan and Southern Rebels Sign Pact to End Civil War
Letter from Syria: Minority activists see beacon in a new Iraq

news.abstract: Pres Bush will increase emergency aid to stricken areas of Asia to $350 million from $35 million; says US will probably add more resources as scope of disaster becomes clearer; UN emergency aid coordinator Jan Egeland says new US money has increased overall amount donated to nearly $1.2 billion from 40 nations; Bush's increase in amount of aid comes after criticism that he had reacted too slowly to disaster (M)
news.title: U.S. Vows Big Increase in Aid for Victims of Asian Disaster

news.abstract: Three Palestinians are killed in Gaza on Dec 31, bringing Palestinian death toll to 12 during latest Israeli military operation to forestall rocket and mortar fire against 21 Israeli settlements; Mahmoud Abbas, leading candidate in Jan 9 presidential election, campaigns in Gaza (M)
news.title: 3 Palestinians Are Killed in Gaza; Candidate Pays a Visit
Israel Raids Gaza, a Week Before Palestinians Vote

news.abstract: The announcement by Asian leaders that they will hold a summit meeting in Jakarta on Thursday to coordinate aid for victims of the tsunami presents the Bush administration with the first of many choices about whether to seize on a disaster to change the nature of how President Bush approaches Asia in his second term.    Until now, the region has fit into Mr. Bush's grand strategy primarily as a second front in his battle against terrorism, and as a place where future conflicts -- with North Korea, between China and Taiwan or India and Pakistan -- must be defused. But beyond that, his agenda has been modest, at best.
news.title: Aid Summit Talks in Jakarta: U.S. Is Facing a Choice and an Opportunity

news.abstract: Officials in charge of the existing international tsunami warning system, which covers only the Pacific Ocean, have taken an initial step to broaden the network to the Indian Ocean and other possible trouble spots, agreeing to distribute their bulletins on earthquakes and possible waves ''to anyone who wants to receive the messages.''     Until now the bulletins had gone only to about 300 agencies and individual scientists tracking conditions mainly in the Pacific, which has historically experienced 90 percent of the world's underwater earthquakes and tsunamis.
news.title: Tsunami Group Will Expand Its Network

news.abstract: Jan Egeland, the United Nations' emergency relief coordinator, said Saturday that the commitment of relief money from more than 40 nations had reached $2 billion, but he said that the scale of the response was overwhelming the capacity to deliver aid.    ''The compassion has never ever been like this,'' he said, but then added, ''The military and civil defense assets that many countries are providing us are as valuable as cash or gold would be today because it makes us move with the assistance and it makes us get there in the race against the clock.''
news.title: With $2 Billion Donated, U.N. Now Needs Help to Deliver Aid

news.abstract: Seen from the air, the Margo desert, which sprawls across the far southwestern corner of Afghanistan toward the borders with Iran and Pakistan, is traced with white car tracks.    With its forbidding reputation as the ''desert of death,'' it deters most travelers but is the favored route of drug traffickers taking opium, heroin and hashish produced in Afghanistan to Iran for smuggling to Turkey and Europe. They cross in armed convoys of 10 to 20 pickup trucks, at such high speed that police officials say they cannot catch them.
news.title: Armed and Elusive, Afghan Drug Dealers Roam Free

news.abstract: Series of murky episodes, including deaths of four North Korean diplomats, have reinforcd sense that North Koreans are less than welcome in Vladivostok, Russia, where 2,500 of them are construction workers; in mid-1990's, Russian authorities were relatively lax about North Korean workers who managed to flee Siberian logging camps; fear now is that collapse of North Korea would bring uncontrolled flood of Korean refugees to region; map (M)
news.title: Russia Turns Sour on North Korean Refugees

news.abstract: Families in many small hamlets in China rely for their prosperity on daughters who go to Thailand and Malaysia to work in brothels; experts say that in some villages, majority of women in their 20's work in this trade, leaving almost no family untouched and young men without mates; photos (M)
news.title: A Village Grows Rich Off Its Main Export: Its Daughters
Kurds seek to maintain a fragile autonomy

news.abstract: Mahmoud Abbas, favorite in impending Palestinian presidential election, visits northern Gaza Strip; calls on militants to stop firing rockets at Israel just hours after latest salvos prompted brief Israeli raid into area; he criticizes both Palestinian rocket fire and Israeli raid; tells militants such attacks are counterproductive (M)
news.title: Candidate Asks Gaza Militants to Stop 'Useless' Attacks on Israelis

news.title: Names of the Dead
For British tabloids, no villain like the EU : Truth, or another media Euromyth?
Ex-Presidents Clinton and Bush to lead major fund-raising push to aid victims : U.S. bolsters call for disaster relief

news.abstract: Prime Min Ayad Allawi telephones Pres Bush and discusses many impediments still facing Iraq as it heads toward elections in 27 days; makes call hours after wave of bombing attacks leaves at least 20 people dead; American officials say Allawi did not say elections should be delayed, but some officials in Washington and in Iraq interpret telephone call as sign that he may be preparing ground to make case for delay to Bush; Allawi is concerned his own party could be headed to defeat if election is held on schedule; his cabinet is already showing signs of weakening on question of holding elections this month; his defense minister Hazem Shaalan has suggested that postponement would encourage Sunnis to participate; American Embassy official says US wants elections to proceed as scheduled; photos (M)
news.title: Iraqi Premier Calls Bush to Discuss Obstacles to Election

news.abstract: American military is considering adding hundreds of military advisers to work directly with Iraqi units, whose disappointing performance could jeopardize long-term American exit strategy from Iraq; new advisers would bolster Iraqi will to fight, help train officers who would lead troops, curb desertion and provide Iraqi forces with confidence that American units would back them up, in some cases fighting alongside them if needed; new advisers would join several hundred American troops already embedded with Iraqi units; embedding more Americans with Iraqis would mean diverting troops away from combat operations, possibly risky move at time when commanders say they need troops to press offensive against insurgents; but plan addresses widely acknowledged need; Pres Bush himself voiced concern about poor performance of Iraqi troops in Dec 20 news conference (M)
news.title: U.S. May Add Advisers to Aid Iraq's Military
Zapatero rejects Basque breakaway

news.abstract: Aboriginal tribes on Andaman and Nicobar Islands in Bay of Bengal largely survived tsunami that devastated coastal areas of archipelago; isolation of six small tribes in highlands may have protected them; Indian government is bringing in aid but continues to bar foreign relief, citing need to protect indigenous tribes; aid groups seek local partners to get around ban; nearly 7,000 people are confirmed dead out of 350,000 on 36 inhabited islands (M)
news.title: Aboriginals Surviving in Highlands

news.abstract: Donors to disaster relief effort in south Asia are often specifying that gifts go exclusively to help those victims (S)
news.title: Giving for a Cause, and That Cause Only
Powell views devastation in hard-hit Indonesian province

news.abstract: South Korea's political and intellectual class turns to looking back, both at military era that ended in 1980's and at Japanese colonial period that ended six decades ago; photos; examinations raise sensitive issues about collaboration with occupiers and, more recently, about responsibility for political assassinations and antidemocratic crackdowns (M)
news.title: Korea's Tricky Task: Digging Up Past Treachery

news.abstract: Americans turn to Internet for word of people who might have fallen victim to tsunami in southern Asia, posting descriptions and mesages on dozens of sites; Internet has also become conduit for big donations to relief organizations (S)
news.title: To Those Seeking Help and Giving It, Computer Is a Lifeline
Firsthand view of disaster
Iraqi leader says vote will be held
Officials gather in Jakarta for tsunami aid talks

news.abstract: General Augusto Pinochet is officially under house arrest at his estate west of Santiago, Chile; is to stand trial for murder and kidnapping that occurred during his 17-year dictatorship; photo (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Americas: Chile: Pinochet Under House Arrest

news.abstract: Breathtaking coastline of South Africa's Eastern Cape, hidden from world for decades under apartheid, has become object of minor land rush by foreign investors; this has touched off emotional debate in country about whether to welcome investors or fend them off with new restrictions on foreign land ownership; government panel formed to investigate issue will deliver interim report this month; nation's blacks, forbidden to own land during apartheid, see hotter property market mainly benefiting South African whites, who could amass property under apartheid; photo; map (M)
news.title: Land Rush by Foreign Investors Divides South Africa

news.abstract: Tsunami left thousands of orphans in its wake in Aceh Province, Indonesia, although numbers of orphans are low because number of children who died was high; rarely was child able to survive where adults could not; photo (M)
news.title: Uncounted Costs: Legions of Orphans and Broken Hearts
Four areas of Iraq too unsafe for voting

news.abstract: Paul A Volcker says report of his investigation into scandal-tainted oil-for-food program in Iraq will not produce any 'smoking gun'; appears to be seeking to lower expectations of what might be in his much-anticipated preliminary report, due this month; program's former director Benon V Sevan has been accused of accepting illegal oil allocations worth millions of dollars, and United Nations Secretary General Kofi Annan has come under personal suspicion because one of contracting companies employed his son Kojo Annan; Volcker's final report is due in June (M)
news.title: No 'Smoking Gun' in the Inquiry Into Iraq's Prewar Oil Sales

news.abstract: Dr Zahi Hawass, Egypt's chief archaeologist, announces removal of King Tut's mummy from tomb at Luxor so scientists can perform three-dimensional CT scan of bones; it is unknown how 17-year-old King Tut died and scans may provide answers about his death; photo (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Middle East: Egypt: CT Scan May Solve Tut Mystery

news.abstract: Veterans of Solidarity movement in Gdansk, Poland, 25 years ago see echoes of their struggle in Ukraine's orange revolution; Solidarity was only self-governing, legally recognized labor union in Soviet bloc in 1981, and thus stakes were higher for pioneering Poles; Ukrainian struggle for democracy enjoys almost automatic support from West, while Western Europe was cautious of Solidarity disturbing detente, although US Pres Reagan supported it; most important similarity is effort to avoid provoking violence; map; photos (M)
news.title: Echo of Gdansk Heard in Ukraine's Shout for Democracy
Sudan Government and Rebels in Deal to End Fighting in South

news.abstract: F-16 fighter mistakenly drops 500-pound bomb on wrong house during attack on insurgents in village of Aitha in northern Iraq, killing at least five Iraqis; owner of house says 14 people, all from same family, died; photo (M)
news.title: U.S. Bombs Wrong House, Killing at Least Five Iraqis

news.abstract: Defense Dept carefully balanced its strategic needs with imperative to open up logistical bottlenecks and begin ferrying water, food, medical supplies and shelter for relief of tsunami victims; has calculated how much combat power it needed to reserve in Pacific to maintain credible deterrent against North Korea and China while sending assistance; Brig Gen Jan-Marc Jouas hopes operation will show world generosity of American people; photo (M)
news.title: Tsunami Tests U.S. Forces' Logistics, but Gives Pentagon a Chance to Show a Human Face

news.abstract: Teams of forensic technicians from 30 countries are working day and night to collect DNA to identify dead from tsunami; Thailand has promised to respect wishes of Western governments to repatriate all identifiable remains of foreigners and none have been cremated; tsunami is believed to have killed hundreds of undocumented workers from Myanmar, complicating matters; map, photos (M)
news.title: Forensic Teams in Thailand Fight Against Heat and Time

news.abstract: American-based private relief agency Mercy Corps starts Cash for Work program in one neighborhood in Banda Aceh, Indonesia, offering men who have lost their homes and livelihoods paid jobs, clearing debris and removing bodies; men clearing debris are paid standard wage for unskilled labor there; those collecting bodies are paid more; it took five days of negotiations before government would sign off on Mercy Corps work program; elsewhere in city, cleanup is being organized by Indonesian military; with shortage of earth-moving equipment and vastness of Aceh Province, job could take months, if not years; this makes Mercy Corps work program useful addition; Mercy Corps hopes to expand program to have 1,000 people in project and expand scope of work to include helping out at local schools; photos (M)
news.title: Indonesian City Gets MoreHelp: $3.30-a-Day Jobs

news.abstract: Independent commission investigating United Nations oil-for-food program in Iraq says UN's auditors did not monitor giant aid effort adequately and that its officials in some cases ignored recommendations that auditors deemed crucial to program's success; commission, lead by Paul A Volcker, issues what it terms 'provisional assessment of auditor performance; release of confidential documents shows loose financial controls over sprawling program, which has become major scandal at UN; there are no allegations of bribery or corruption by UN officials, but audits make clear that many of deficiencies were known in late 1990's, at time when indications of corruption of program by Saddam Hussein and others were also reaching UN; commission notes auditors' failure to monitor in depth New York headquarters of office that administered program, or to monitor contracts for oil sales that provided revenue for program or those for purchase of relief and other goods supposed to ease effect of sanctions on Iraqis; commission notes that program suffered from 'chronic shortage' of auditors (M)
news.title: Report From Panel Shows Lapses In U.N.'s Oil-for-Food Program
New premier is picked forSerb-run half of Bosnia
Pact ends one of Sudan's civil wars
But country won't be less secure, he asserts : Powell admits to concern over a postelection Iraq
Italy's ban on smokinggets off to a fuming start
U.S. Agrees to Release Last 4 Britons From Guantanamo Prison

news.abstract: China has spent fortune assembling one of world's largest passenger airline fleets; it transported 80 million passengers last year, fourfold increase from 1991; front line workers in country's mass air-travel revolution are China's flight attendants, most of them women; they like job's middle class wages, but work shifts are brutal, and they must deal with intemperate passengers; there is little regulation of working conditions; one trouble-laden flight described; photo (M)
news.title: Bedlam in the Air for China Flight Attendants

news.abstract: Along coast of southern Thailand, schools face challenge not only of rounding up displaced children and finding new quarters, but of helping pupils deal with emotional toll of devastating tsunami; some are orphans, and mmny more lost either mother or father; photo (M)
news.title: Routine Helps Students Deal With Wave's Toll
Rebel sally kills 19 in Philippines

news.abstract: In a major security breach, a Pakistani man sentenced to death for trying to assassinate President Pervez Musharraf in 2003 has escaped from prison, officials disclosed, and a nationwide hunt is under way. The man, Mushtaq Ahmed, escaped from an air force jail in the northern city of Rawalpindi on Nov. 25 when he was allowed to take a bath and his guard fell asleep, according to an initial report. He had been sentenced to death in the Dec. 14, 2003, assassination attempt against General Musharraf -- the first of two attempts that month -- when a bridge blew up seconds after his motorcade passed by. No one was hurt.   Salman Masood (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Pakistan: Musharraf Bomber On The Run

news.abstract: US agrees to release last four Britons and one Australian who have been held without charge at Guantanamo Bay Naval Base for around three years; US statement says Britain and Australia have accepted responsibility to prevent suspects from engaging in terrorist activities in future; Sec Jack Straw says British police will decide whether to arrest them again; photos (M)
news.title: 4 Britons and an Australian to Be Freed at Guantánamo

news.abstract: US and Russia are close to agreement on curbing trafficking in shoulder-fired antiaircraft missiles often used by terrorists; Min Sergei B Ivanov and Sec Donald Rumsfeld detail accord at news conference in Washington (M)
news.title: U.S. and Russia Seeking Limits on Portable Antiaircraft Missiles

news.abstract: Jan Egeland of UN says donor countries have pledged $717 million to UN appeal for emergency help for ten Asian countries hit by earthquake and tsunami (S)
news.title: $717 Million Pledged to U.N. Aid Effort

news.abstract: President Vladimir V. Putin vetoed a new law restricting the sale and public consumption of beer. The restrictions were adopted by the upper and lower houses of Parliament last year as part of a legislative assault on beer, which until now has not been covered by laws regulating sales and advertising of wine and hard liquor and as a result has become ubiquitous on city streets across Russia. In a letter to lawmakers, Mr. Putin criticized the law for a lack of specifics and suggested that local governments should be empowered to draft their own restrictions on public places where beer drinking would be banned.   Steven Lee Myers (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Russia: Putin Vetoes Beer Ban

news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Germany: 22 Islamic Suspects Held In Raids
Blair defends laws allowing pubs to stay open past 11

news.abstract: Chilean appeals court approves $3,500 bail for 89-year-old former dictator Gen Augusto Pinochet, who has been under house arrest charged with kidnapping and murder stemming from his time as Chilean leader (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Americas: Chile: Bail For Pinochet

news.abstract: Indonesia announces that all foreign troops assisting in tsunami relief operation must leave by late March; government is sensitive to impression that it is relying too heavily on outside military forces; number of countries, including United States, have sent or are sending troops to help; Indonesia military has fought civil war against separatist rebels in Aceh Province for 30 years and has kept Aceh virtually sealed to outsiders in that period; photo (M)
news.title: Indonesia Orders Foreign Troops Providing Aid to Leave by March 26
Sharon Cuts Israeli Ties With Palestinian Authority

news.abstract: Project and Contracting Office, formed by Pentagon to oversee $18.4 billion program to rebuild Iraq's physical infrastructure, will begin handing its responsibilities over to United States Army Corps of Engineers over next several months; Charles Hess, director of office, denies that move is response to Iraqi and American criticism that reconstruction effort focused too much on large projects, started up too slowly and failed to anticipate attacks by insurgents; defends reconstruction program as successful, given hard realities of Iraq (M)
news.title: U.S. Army to Expand Role in Iraq's Civil Engineering

news.abstract: Indonesian coastal town of Calang, where thousands of people were swept away by tsunami, has not just been destroyed, it has vanished; most of town's 7.300 people are missing; only 323 bodies have been found; Calang and many other villages on western coast of Aceh Province have been wiped from map; suffering along land closest to earthquake's epicenter has been compounded by its remoteness; devastation is great and numbers in need is huge; much of terrain is accessible only by helicopter; photos; map (M)
news.title: Once a Village, Now Nothing: Even the Bodies Are Gone

news.abstract: American Amb B Lynn Pascoe says United States is not troubled by Indonesian government's demands that aid workers in Aceh Province register and that all foreign troops be gone by end of March; describes restrictions as 'reasonable'; Indonesian government has said its curbs on aid workers in Aceh, which has been torn by civil war for 30 years, are necessary for their protection; pohto (M)
news.title: U.S. Calls Indonesia Deadline for Troop Pullout Reasonable
Re-election strategy also includes reform: Blair turns focus to prosperity

news.abstract: Pres Hugo Chavez of Venezuela suspends bilateral accords and commercial relations with Colombia until government in Bogota apologizes for its role in capture of rebel commander in Caracas (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Americas: Venezuela: Chávez Ends Accords With Colombia

news.abstract: China, in its seemingly bottomless demand for electricity, plans to build nuclear power reactors on scale and pace comparable to most ambitious nuclear energy programs world has ever seen; current plans call for new reactors to be commissioned at rate of nearly two a year between 2005 and 2020; China's eight nuclear reactors supply less than 2 percent of nation's current demand; critics question whether such small payoff warrants exposure to risk of catastrophic failures, nuclear proliferation, terrorism and unresolved problems of radioactive waste disposal; map; photo shows control room of China's nuclear power plant in Daya Bay (M)
news.title: China Promotes Another Boom: Nuclear Power

news.abstract: World Trade Organization dir gen Supachai Panitchpakdi issues plea to member nations to lower trade barriers as way of helping nations ravaged by tsunami (M)
news.title: Rich Nations Are Urged to Ease Trade With Affected Countries

Six-party talks may resume within weeks, U.S. says: N. Korea will return to nuclear discussions

news.abstract: Lt Gen John R Vines, who will take over in mid-February as American ground commander in Iraq, says main job after elections will be to improve training of Iraqi security forces; as many as 10,000 American military advisors could be assigned to work directly with Iraqi units; Vines has assigned his commanders and senior officers reading list on Islam and brought in Islamic scholars to help them understand culture and region; photos (M)
news.title: New U.S. Commander Sees Shift in Military Role in Iraq

news.abstract: Profile of Dr Khunying Porntip Rojanasunan, deputy director of Thailand's Central Institute of Forensic Science; purple-haired former movie star has been directing post-tsunami forensic operation at Yan Yao temple, but she has been criticized for not following international procedures for identifying dead; Thai officials have ordered that 800 bodies sent to cemetery for burial be returned to temple morgue for further testing and to make sure no foreigners are among them; police will take over identification process and at least 2,000 unidentified bodies will be retested; map; photo (M)
news.title: Thai Doctor Fashions a Life Working Among the Dead

news.abstract: European Space Agency spacecraft Huygens lands on Saturn's moon Titan and shows pictures of drainage channels running to mysterious shoreline; flat dark areas could be lakes of liquid methane or just flat surface of dark material; craft sends back data and images for one hour and ten minutes; effort is hampered by loss of one communication channel for transmitting data to Cassini mother ship, cutting number of pictures to 350 from planned 700, but mission is considered success; photo (M)
news.title: Titan's Big News: A Mysterious Shoreline
Bush Signals Steadfast Approach to Iraq
Estonian Wind Farm Now Grows Where Soviet Guards Trained

news.abstract: Article, Back Channels, recounts how Ukraine's intelligence services thwarted military crackdown against democracy demonstrators massed in Kiev last November; senior intelligence officials warned Interior Ministry that using force against peaceful rallies was illegal and said army and security services would defend civilians against ministry troops; exchanges among top officials were hidden factor in Orange Revolution that overturned fraudulent election and changed Ukraine's political course, and are rare in former Soviet states where security agencies are often most conservative, ruthless instruments of state power; inside battle was waged by clique of top officials, known as siloviki, who chose not to follow Pres Leonid Kuchma's plan to pass power to Prime Min Viktor Yanukovich; Oleksander Galaka, head of military intelligence, and Col Gen Ihor P Smeshko were among those warning Lt Gen Sergei Popkov not to send in Interior Ministry troops; officers also funneled information to opposition led by Viktor Yushchenko and engaged in psychological tug-of-war to soften government response to protests; group also included Lt Gen Lt Gen Oleksander Skibinetsky and Lt Gen Oleksander Skipalsky, who had relatives in crowds; photos; day-by-day developments recounted (L)
news.title: How Top Spies in Ukraine Changed the Nation's Path

news.abstract: Prime Min Ariel Sharon, in blunt warning to new Palestinian leader, warns Mahmoud Abbas that Israeli military will act 'without restrictions' against Palestinians stepping up attacks in Gaza; PLO issues rare call for halt to 'all military acts' that provide 'excuses' to Israel, reflecting efforts of Abbas, who is also PLO chairman; Hamas renews rocket and mortar fire in Gaza; Israeli gunfire reportedly kills two Palestinians; Israeli troops pull back from outskirts of Gaza City after clashes in which eight Palestinians are killed, most of them militants; photo; Palestinian shelling wounds two Israeli children at Gaza settlement and teenage girl in Sederot (M)
news.title: Sharon Orders New Crackdown on Gaza Factions

news.abstract: Lists of millions of registered Iraqi voters are being sent to election officials in Baghdad and will be posted at district offices around country; UN oficial Carlos Valenzuela says workers are close to settling on more than 5,000 polling places; election timetable; US forces continue raids in Mosul and Kirkuk, finding weapons caches and insurgents; photos; Valenzuela also reports eight election workers killed; denies mass resignations in Mosul and Anbar (M)
news.title: High-Ranking Officers May Face Prosecution in Iraqi Prisoner Abuse, Military Officials Say
China Curbs Discussion of Late Leader Who Opposed Crackdown

news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Ministers Say I.R.A. Robbed Belfast Bank

news.abstract: Palestinian Authority's new president Mahmoud Abbas orders his security forces to try to prevent attacks against Israel; move could put him on collision course with armed Palestinian factions; he will not give details about how security forces might act against militant groups, and there is no sign that any action has started; Abbas has publicly opposed attacks on Israel as counterproductive, but genuine crackdown on Hamas, Islamic Jihad and other groups that have sworn to continue their attacks could put him in full-fledged confrontation with them; solid majority of Palestinians support suicide bombings and shootings to oppose Israeli occupation in West Bank and Gaza and to fight for statehood, although there are signs that support has declined as violence grinds on; photo (M)
news.title: Abbas Tells Palestinian Forces to Block Attacks on Israel

news.abstract: United Nations-sponsored international team says drastically reducing poverty in its many guises--hunger, illiteracy, disease--is 'utterly affordable' if industrial nations agree to double aid to poor countries, to one-half of 1 percent of national incomes, or 50 cents out of every $100 of incomes; report by so-called United Nations Millennium Project advocates reforms to ease trade barriers and sweeping investments in health, education, rural development, road building, housing and scientific research; blueprint wins quick praise from heads of International Monetary Fund and World Bank; some critics view its approach as utopian overreaching; others worry that it puts too little emphasis on need for poor countries to make deep political and social changes to reduce poverty; project's agenda is first in series this year intended to refocus attention on fulfilling promises to fight poverty that were made at UN in 2000; photos (M)
news.title: U.N. Panel Urges Doubling of Aid to Cut Poverty

news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Ukraine: Inauguration Clears A Hurdle

news.abstract: Insurgents in Iraq release Syrian Catholic archbishop, Basile Georges Casmoussa, day after he was snatched from streets of Mosul; new hostage drama pens as eight Chinese construction workers are shown on video, held at gunpoint by masked men; interior minister Falah Hassan al-Naqib warns Iraq will tear itself apart unless enough people vote in election; Amb John Negroponte says elections can be successful, while admitting there is no end in sight to insurgency and US does not know how big it is; international group reports 18,000 Iraqi expatriates in 14 countries have registered to vote so far; US soldier is killed by bomb in Baghdad, second in western Iraq; three political candidates reported killed; photos of Iraqi girl screaming after parents are killed when US soldiers fire on car when it failed to stop, and of British soldier feigning punch at bound Iraqi prisoner (M)
news.title: Archbishop Freed in Iraq, but 8 Chinese Are Captives

news.abstract: New US intelligence estimates reportedly predict that post-election government in Iraq will almost certainly ask US to set specific timetable for withdrawing troops; reports, which assume Shiite election win, see even more violence, including Shiite-Sunni clashes that could lead to civil war; request would put new pressure on Bush administration to speed training of Iraqi forces able to confront insurgency; grim tone of new assessments comes as officials like Sec Colin Powell acknowledge that 'raging insurgency' is not likely to fade soon (M)
news.title: U.S. Intelligence Says Iraqis Will Press for Withdrawal

Rice gets skeptical questions at hearing

news.abstract: British military authorities and politicians seek to limit public debate about allegations that three British soldiers abused Iraqi prisoners shortly after they occupied Basra in 2003; there is widening revulsion in other European countries; men are being court-martialed in Germany; Prime Min Tony Blair moves swiftly to try to prevent scandal from adding to political costs of Britain's deployment in Iraq; he and his adversaries in Parliament seem united in ascribing abuses in Basra to tiny minority of British troops (M)
news.title: Britain Tries to Tone Down Debate Over Prisoner Abuse
British Major Denies Abuse of Iraqis

news.abstract: Washington Post publishes follow-up article questioning earlier article about claims by Jumana Michael Hanna, Iraqi woman, about her horrific torture at hands of Saddam Hussein's regime; Hanna's tale was unusual in that she was willing to name Iraqi police officials who participated in her alleged rape and torture over two-year period of imprisonment; she was granted refugee status by United States officials on basis of her claims; articles in Esquire magazine and Post now conclude that none of her allegations could be verified; apparent debunking of her story raises questions about her embrace by officials from Coalition Provisional Authority in 2003 (M)
news.title: Iraqi Refugee's Tale of Abuse Dissolves Upon Later Scrutiny

news.abstract: Ukraine's Parliament votes to inaugurate Viktor A Yushchenko as country's next president on Jan 23, nearly three months after first votes were cast; inauguration will end electoral crisis that prompted huge public demonstrations and behind-the-scenes intrigue, deeply dividing country and souring its relations with Russia; Pres Vladimir V Putin, who had supported Yushchenko's opponent Viktor F Yanukovich, congratulates Yushchenko in statement passed through diplomatic channels, rather than telephone call; Yushchenko's upcoming trip to Moscow will be test of his ability to overcome bitterness caused by what many of his supporters saw as Russian interference in campaign; Yushchenko intends to tour Europe after his Russian visit, underscoring his efforts to balance relations between Russia and West (M)
news.title: Yushchenko Set for Oath This Sunday

news.abstract: United States pledges to expand emergency tsunami and earthquake warning system to cover globe; Japan promises to start immediately stitching together emergency warning system for Indian Ocean (M)
news.title: U.S. Vows to Attain Global Warning System
ECB fight pits small against big

news.abstract: Earlier this month, according to Iraqi officials, $300 million in American bills was taken out of Iraq's Central Bank, put into boxes and quietly put on a charter jet bound for Lebanon.    The money was to be used to buy tanks and other weapons from international arms dealers, the officials say, as part of an accelerated effort to assemble an armored division for the fledgling Iraqi Army. But exactly where the money went, and to whom, and for precisely what, remains a mystery, at least to Iraqis who say they have been trying to find out.

news.abstract: United Nations' top human rights official Louise Arbour says any delay in prosecuting war crimes from Darfur region of Sudan would risk lives and end hope of forging eventual peace; statement intensifies pressure on United States to put aside its opposition to International Criminal Court; UN human rights commission has given Secretary Gen Kofi Annan list of 51 names of suspects and evidence against them (M)

news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Nepal: Calls To Block Military Aid

news.abstract: Five suicide bombers, some disguised in robes of religious pilgrims, explode their bombs in crowds of worshipers and at police check point in Baghdad area, killing at least 35 people on eve of Shiite holy day of Ashura; explosions raise fears of repeat of last year's carnage, when about 180 people were killed during Ashura celebrations; photos (M)
news.title: Suicide Bombers Kill at Least 35 in Baghdad Area

news.abstract: UN High Commissioner for Refugees Ruud Lubbers refuses to step down over sexual harassment charges; Lubbers emerges from talks with Sec Gen Kofi Annan and denies that his resignation had been discussed; dismisses his accusers as liars and attacks UN for slandering him; Lubbers photo (M)
news.title: U.N. Official Rejects Calls to Step Down Under Fire

news.abstract: Far-right Israelis grow increasingly strident in lead-up to planned withdrawal of Israeli settlers from Gaza Strip this summer; many people draw parallel to period preceding assassination of Prime Min Yitzhak Rabin in 1995 and fear for Prime Min Ariel Sharon's safety; some senior officials call for pre-emptive steps like administrative detention without trial, legal step rarely used against Israelis; protests assume aggressive edge, but leaders of organized opposition in Gaza and West Bank say they reject violence; photo (M)
news.title: Israel Gears Up for Burst of Far-Right Anger
China Denounces United States-Japan Agreement on Taiwan

news.abstract: Hundreds of people gather in Great Britain on horseback and foot to ride and run with hounds in defiance of new law forbidding hunting with intent to kill foxes and allowing hounds to do killing; hunters insist they will test law without actually breaking it, under legal guise of exercising hounds; some see situation as crisis of confidence in government; others say fight is urban-rural battle or class warfare; photos (M)
news.title: Testing New Ban, Britons Run With the Hounds

news.abstract: Six suicide bombers attack crowds in Iraq celebrating Shiite holiday Ashura, killing as many as 39 people and injuring about 150 others; group led by Abu Musab al-Zarqawi claims responsibility for suicide bombing outside Iraqi Army building in Baquba; American soldier is killed in attacks near Kadimain shrine; bomber on bicycle rides into tent of Sunni mourners at funeral in Baghdad, mistaking them for Shiites; photos (M)
news.title: Suicide Bombers Aim at a Shiite Holy Day in Iraq

news.abstract: New threat of terrorism from within exposes tension between Islamic politicians and pro-Western liberals in Kuwait; crisis began on Jan 10 when police uncovered suspected Al Qaeda cell planning attacks on American troops and various sites; gun battles followed on Jan 30 and Jan 31; analysts say government was caught off-guard at critical moment, as Emir Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah and Crown Prince Sheik Saad al-Abdullah al-Sabah are both ill and power vacuum looms; photo (M)
news.title: Internal Tension Simmers in Kuwait as Islamic Politicians Clash With Pro-Westerner Liberals

news.abstract: Winnipeg's American Hockey League team, high-scoring Manitoba Moose, emerges as hottest box office draw of any professional hockey team in Canada; city has not had NHL game since 1996, when Winnipeg Jets left for Phoenix; photos; map (M)
news.title: Who Needs the N.H.L. When the Moose Is on the Loose?

news.abstract: Royal Navy begins actively encouraging gays to enlist and pledges to make life easier when they do, five years after Britain lifted its ban on gays in military; navy says it has asked Stonewall, group that lobbies for gay rights, to help it develop better strategies for recruiting and retaining gay men and lesbians, possibly by advertising in gay mgazines and newspapers; new effort continues pattern of changing official attitudes in navy dating to 1999, when European court ruled that Britain's ban on gays in military violated European human-rights laws; gays in British miltary are subject to same rules of sexual conduct as heterosexuals: no touching, no kissing, no flaunting of sexuality; despite change in policy, relatively few gay men and lesbians already in military have come out (M)
news.title: New Course by Royal Navy: A Campaign to Recruit Gays
World Briefings
Landslide in Portugal

news.abstract: Afghanistan is well behind its neighbors in several indicators of poverty and vulnerability in latest United Nations Human Development Index; report warns that country could revert to anarchy if its dire poverty, poor health and insecurity are not improved; report notes that despite its massive problems, Afghanistan has shown remarkable progress in three years since United States-led war in 2001 drove out Taliban; photo; chart (M)
news.title: Afghan Living Standards Among the Lowest, U.N. Finds

news.abstract: Syrian Pres Bashar al-Assad repeats longstanding promise to withdraw his troops from Lebanon, as tens of thousands of people march through streets of Beirut in largest anti-Syrian protests since killing of former Prime Min Rafik Hariri week ago; political analysts dismiss Assad's pledge, made to Arab League secretary general Amr Moussa, as mere wordplay; hours after Moussa reports on pledge, Syrian government seeks to minimize its effects; opposition figures say Syrian control over Lebanon is so tight that it can easily make promises without fear of ever having to make good on them; photo (M)
news.title: Syria Pledges Pullout Again Amid Protests by Lebanese
Mayor unrepentant after Nazi remarks

news.abstract: State Department and Pentagon officials express renewed concern that Nicaragua may not destroy its arsenal of portable antiaircraft missiles as it promised during Defense Sec Donald H Rumsfeld's visit to Managua in 2004; American delegation is in Managua to renew pressure on Nicaraguan government to destroy all of shoulder-fired missiles supplied by Cuba and Soviet Union during 1980's (M)
news.title: Nicaragua Lags on Vow to Scrap Portable Missiles
Iceland to Grant Passport to Fischer

Pope's book creates quick controversy

news.abstract: Canadian government refuses to take part in planned North America missile defense system despite personal lobbying by Pres Bush there in Nov; long-awaited decision from Prime Min Paul Martin is symbolic setback for Bush administration as it tries to heal rifts with allies emerging from invasion of Iraq; administration officials say Canada's decision will not deter United States; Martin had supported Canada's participation in missile defense program before he became Liberal Party leader in 2003; he reversed his position amid strong opposition from backbench Liberal Party members in House of Commons, and polls showing system to be unpopular with public (M)
news.title: Canada Says It Won't Join Missile Shield With the U.S.
Karzai visits India to bolster economic ties
In Belarus and Moldova, hopes for democracy

news.abstract: Two British soldiers are convicted of abusing Iraqi detainees by military jury in Germany in case widely known as Britain's Abu Ghraib; third soldier has pleaded guilty; incidents all took place in May 2003 during operation to stop looting at aid depot near Basra; abuse came to light after one soldier, having returned home, dropped off roll of photographs at shop showing naked Iraqi detainees in humiliating sexual poses (M)
news.title: 2 British Soldiers Convicted of Abusing Prisoners in Iraq

news.abstract: Benon V Sevan, former head of United Nations Oil-for-Food program, asks for extention to respond to charges filed two weeks ago that claim he helped friend obtain contracts through program; Fred Eckhard, spokesman for United Nations Sec Gen Kofi Annan, says request is being considered (S)
news.title: World Briefing | United Nations: Oil-For-Food Figure Seeks Extension

news.abstract: Colima, Mexico, Governor Gustavo Vazquez Montes, three aides and two pilots are killed when state-owned jet crashes into mountains near Tzitzio town; cause of crash is unknown (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Americas: Mexico: Jet Crash Kills Governor

news.title: Bush and Putin on Democracy, Political Debate and Iraq

news.abstract: Vatican says Pope John Paul II appears to be recovering from tracheotomy; denies reports that pope had been attached to ventilator, and says procedure was elective; medical experts say tracheotomy poses new dangers for pope; his health has been fragile for years, but question of his ability to lead church has been taboo; this second hospitalization is forcing Vatican officials and Roman Catholics around world to come to grips with what may be much-changed papacy; photos (M)
news.title: Pope Described As Recovering After Surgery

news.abstract: Faure Gnassingbe bows to international pressure and will step down three weeks after military installed him to succeed his late father, Gnassingbe Eyadema, as Togo's president; he will be replaced by Abass Bonfo, member of Parliament, who will become interim president and oversee elections within 60 days (M)
news.title: Togo Ruler, Surrendering to Pressure, Steps Down

news.abstract: Judge in Cairo's Family Court orders DNA test to settle unprecedented paternity suit that has riveted Egyptians for months; Hind el-Hinnawy has sued actor Ahmed el-Fishawy, saying he fathered her four-month-old girl during their secret marriage (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Middle East: Egypt: DNA Test Ordered In Paternity Case
African Union demands that Togo's army-installed leader resign

news.abstract: Report by Justice Dept Inspector Gen Glenn A Fine says that dozens of subcontractors hired in 2003 to help Iraq rebuild its prison system did not undergo thorough background checks into allegations of misconduct by some of them at US prisons; concludes that none of their backgrounds would have disqualified them from working in Iraq and that none of them were involved in abuses at Abu Ghraib prison; report was prompted by request for investigation from Sen Charles E Schumer (M)
news.title: Flaws Reported in Screening Subcontractors for Iraq Prisons

news.abstract: Kurdish leaders say they will write into new Iraqi Constitution system granting considerable powers to individual regions and legitimizing their use of militia called pesh merga; about 100,000 pesh merga would nominally fall under Defense Ministry in Baghdad, but really be controlled by regional commanders; major Shiite parties may try to block Kurdish autonomy; American commanders argue that all militias must be state-sponsored and not organized by ethnicity or sect; photo (M)
news.title: Kurds Vow to Retain Militia as Guardians of Autonomy

news.abstract: Career officers at Central Intelligence Agency fear prosecution and punishment for conduct during interrogations and detentions of terrorism suspects; several cases are currently under review by Justice Dept; concern in ranks has been growing since removal of Baghdad station chief in December 2003 because of concerns about deaths of two Iraqis questioned by CIA employees (M)
news.title: Within C.I.A., Worry of Prosecution for Conduct

news.abstract: In wake of Pope John Paul II's tracheotomy, after second trip in one month to hospital, there is sense in Rome that significant corner has been turned in his long public illness, but it has not yet manifested itself openly as vigil; Pope will not take part in today's weekly public Angelus blessing and prayer for what seems to be first time in 26 years, but he reportedly is otherwise in good condition; photo (M)
news.title: Crowds at St. Peter's Are on Tours, Not a Papal Death Watch

news.abstract: Egyptian Pres Hosni Mubarak asks Parliament to amend Constitution to allow direct, multiparty presidential elections for first time; some opposition politicians and analysts hail proposal, while skeptics await details; proponents regard move as first step in reviewing entire Constitution and response to domestic Bush administration pressure; Egypt's Parliament has long history of diluting reforms; recent arrest of Ayman Nour, leader of newly formed opposition party, seems at odds with Mubarak's commitment to democracy; photos (M)
news.title: Mubarak Pushes Egypt to Allow Freer Elections

news.abstract: Islamic Jihad claims responsibility for suicide bombing in Tel Aviv; says one-month pause in attacks is over and will not be extended because Israel has continued to arrest and kill Palestinians; Israel blames Syria for supporting Islamic Jihad, and Israeli and Palestinian security forces each make arrests in West Bank; Palestinian Pres Mahmoud Abbas, speaking before Islamic Jihad's claim, explicitly condemns bombing (M)
news.title: Islamic Jihad Says It WasBehind Tel Aviv Bombing

news.abstract: Croatian Foreign Min Kolinda Grabar-Kitarovic says European Union is making impossible demand in requiring that war crimes suspect be turned over to international tribunal at The Hague as condition for starting negotiations on membership; contends that there is no evidence that Gen Ante Gotovina is in Croatia, although tribunal says he is; Western diplomats say Croatia is not doing everything it can to comply (M)
news.title: Europe Union Upsets Croatia With Demands

news.abstract: Pres Hosni Mubarak's unexpected announcement that Egypt will hold its first direct, multiparty presidential election is seen by commentators as important, if small, step on road to reform; they expect no sweepingg change from Mubarak, noting he has spent 24 years making sure nothing ruffles political life in Egypt (M)
news.title: A Qualified Welcome for Mubarak Proposal

news.abstract: French Parliament clears way for referendum on European Union's new consitution; Pres Jacques Chirac will meet with leaders to determine date for vote; eight other countries will vote on constitution, while remaining nations will ratify document by parliamentary vote (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: France: Ready To Vote On Constitution

news.abstract: Uruguay will join other Latin American nations in new leftist consensus as it prepares to inaugurate Tabare Vazquez as president; three-quarters of nations are governed by left-leaning leaders, all of whom have emerged in past six years and are redefining what left means; tide is not so much doctrinaire as pragmatic; leaders are different in style and substance, but united in conviction that free-market reforms of 1990's have failed and by renewed focus on egalitarianism and social welfare; attitude toward United States is one of polite distancing, as economic reforms being rejected are closely associated with Washington and financial institutions it backs; critics on left decry middle ground as sellout but others see it as maturing into mainstream; photos (M)
news.title: With New Chief, Uruguay Veers Left, in a Latin Pattern
Tsunami aid arriving with rare speed

news.abstract: Iraqi judge and lawyer with special tribunal that will try Saddam Hussein and former members of his government are shot to death outside their home in Baghdad; Parwiz Muhammad Mahmoud al-Merani and son, who worked at tribunal, are killed day after first charges are announced; senior Iraqi official says Hussein's half brother was captured by Iraqi and allied forces, not by Syria; some 400 tribunal members have security guards and names are kept secret; seven Iraqi police officers are killed in four incidents, day after bombing in Hilla that killed at least 122 people and wounded 170 more; photo; Abu Musab al-Zarqawi terrorists claim responsibility; Muslim Scholars Assn, influential Sunni group, denounces Hilla attack; French reporter Florence Aubenas, kidnapped Jan 5, appeals for help on videotape (M)

news.abstract: Indonesian court acquits radical Islamic cleric Abu Bakar Bashir of all terrorism charges in bombings in Marriott Hotel in Jakarta in Aug 2003, and of having directed bombings of nightclubs in Bali in Oct 2002; for more than two years, Bush administration has pressed Indonesian government to prosecute man they portray as Osama bin Laden's lieutenant in Southeast Asia; in what appears to be concession to American pressure, five judges convict Bashir of one of eight counts, criminal conspiracy in Bali bombings, saying his words may have encouraged perpetrators, whom he knew; prosecution's case was hampered because Bush adminstration refused to make available to Indonesians two importat al Qaeda members now in American custody, Riudan Isamuddin and Omar al-Faruq (M)
news.title: Radical Cleric in Indonesia Is Acquitted of Terrorism

news.abstract: Pedophile case involving 66 adults accused of abusing 45 children opens in Angers, France, setting off national debate about erosion of moral values and state's ability to protect underprivileged children; trial involves 39 men and 27 women charged with rape or selling their children for sex; nearly all come from French underclass; case came to light while police were monitoring convicted sex offender; lawyers say case is much stronger than sordid pedophile trial of 18 people in city of Outreau year ago; that case ended with suicide and 10 convictions after central defendant suddenly retracted her story implicating other defendants in abuse of at least 18 children, leaving many people uncertain of guilt of some of those convicted (M)
news.title: A Shaken France Watches as a Vast Pedophile Trial Begins

news.abstract: Take Back Your Time and various advocacy groups say too many workers feel overstressed by demands on their time and are arguing for more paid time off to allow them to devote more time to their families; Democrats plan to introduce bill guaranteeing seven paid days off each year for when workers or children are ill; Pres Bush and allies favor twice-failed bill offering overtime workers choice between  Middle East enters uncharted political and social territory with mixture of anticipation and dread following opening of Egyptian elections to multiple candidates fall of Lebanese government before street demonstrators and limited vote for municipal councils in Saudi Arabia ; uncensored satellite television spurs protests and pressure from Bush administration emboldens them; American campaign for democracy in Middle East is viewed by many as anti-Arab conspiracy; photo (M)

news.abstract: Navalady in eastern Sri Lanka, lost at least 620 of about 1,900 inhabitants in tsunami, including wife and four sons of bodybuilder Santosh Chinnathambi Selvam; most of 490 families were related in one way or another; residents waver between vowing never to return and saying they would return if everyone else did; community spirit frayed during refuge at school in Batticaloa, yet according to Hindu custom 30 days after disaster, people returned to Navalady to cook feast for their relatives who had died; photos; map (L)
news.title: Torn From Moorings, Villagers From Sri Lanka Grasp for Past

news.abstract: Sinn Fein leader Gerry Adams uses keynote address at party's annual conference to reiterate party's rejection of criminal activity after months of accusations linking Irish Republican Army and Sinn Fein to bank robberies, money-laundering and murder; promises justice to family of murdered man Robert McCartney although intimidation has stopped all 72 witnesses from giving evidence to police; speech is largely devoted to criticism of Britain, Ireland and Protestant rivals in Northern Ireland (M)
news.title: Sinn Fein Leader Reasserts Rejection of Criminal Activity
China slaps at U.S. on North Korea

news.abstract: Police in Taiwan say they identified man who shot and injured Pres Chen Shui-bian on eve of national elections year ago; say he drowned himself days after shooting, leaving suicide note that blamed Chen for his financial problems but did not take responsibility for shooting; national sympathy for Chen after shooting helped him win re-election; opposition party figures cast doubt on police story and say they will hold demonstration on anniversary of attack (M)
news.title: Taiwan Police Say Who Shot President, but Suspect Is Dead

news.abstract: Anger is growing in Italy over killing of Italian intelligence officer by American military in Iraq; pressure on Prime Min Silvio Berlusconi to withdraw Italy's 3,000 troops in Iraq is expected to mount; murkiness of details about shooting is also stoking anger; photo (M)
news.title: U.S. Killing of Italian Officer Stokes Anger Against War

news.abstract: Hans A Bethe, who discovered violent reactions behind sunlight, led theoreticians who devised atom bomb and then fought many new weapons of cold war, dies at age 98, last of giants who inaugurated nuclear age; Bethe, who fled Germany in 1930's, pioneered some of most esoteric realms of physics and astrophysics, long advising federal government and in time emerging as science community's liberal conscience; 1938 paper on how sun and similar stars fuse hydrogen into helium, releasing bursts of energy and light, helped establish his reputation as father of nuclear astrophysics and earned him Nobel Prize in 1967; photos; diagram; Bethe was last of greats who led Manhattan Project, outliving not only his conservative counterpoint Edward Teller but also Enrico Fermi and J Robert Oppenheimer (M)
news.title: Hans Bethe, Prober of Sunlight and Atomic Energy, Dies at 98

news.abstract: Al Ameen electrical substation in eastern Baghdad is dedicated, reflecting new US and Iraqi focus on individual neighborhoods after nearly two years of concentrating on enormous power plants and high-tension cables; Al Ameen distribution center that will siphon energy from national grid and spread it around districts where aging equipment constantly breaks down (M)
news.title: Next Step in Rebuilding Iraq: Bring Power to the People

news.abstract: Pres Bush chooses John R Bolton, blunt-spoken conservative known for sharp skepticism of UN, as US ambassador to world body; photo; Sec Condoleezza Rice says he is tough-minded diplomat with track record of effective multilateralism who will speak with strong voice, as did some of well-known predecessors; 56-year-old lawyer has worked in federal government for most of last 25 years, lately as under secretary of state for arms control and international security; choice is lauded by conservatives and criticized by UN diplomats; Vice Pres Cheney reportedly pushed him for post (M)
news.title: Bush Nominates Weapons Expert as Envoy to U.N.

news.abstract: Long-awaited official report on Israeli government's support for illegal settlements in West Bank describes widespread state complicity, fraud and cynicism, illegal diversion of funds and seizure of private Palestinian land; report by former chief prosecutor Talia Sasson was commissioned under US pressure and delivered to Prime Min Ariel Sharon, whose government is accused of 'blatant violations of law' in helping settlers set up illegal outposts (M)
news.title: Israeli Report Condemns Support for Settlement Outposts

news.title: American Doctors Helped Identify Ukraine Leader's Poisoning

news.abstract: Iraqi Deputy Minister of Industry Sami al-Araji says after fall of Baghdad looters systematically dismantled and removed tons of machinery from most important weapons installations, including some with high-precision equipment capable of making parts for nuclear arms; facilities were left largely unguarded by allied forces; peak of organized looting was from mid-April to mid-May of 2003 as teams with flatbed trucks and heavy equipment moved systematically from site to site; United Nations has been hunting for equipment unsuccessfully across Middle East; photos; map (L)
news.title: Looting at Weapons Plants Was Systematic, Iraqi Says

news.abstract: As India and Pakistan face off in Mohali, India, for first test match of six-week cricket series, Indians and Pakistanis greet each other with mixture of emotions; Pakistani Pres Pervez Musharraf is expected to attend a match, probably in Indian city of Kochi, adding explicitly political flavor to game; last year's match took Indian team to Pakistan and prompted effusion of hospitality; this year's match occurs amid peace talks that have led to cooperation between two countries on Kashmir issue; photos; map (M)
news.title: A Cricket Match Bridges a Longtime Gap in Punjab

news.abstract: Terje Roed-Larson, special United Nations envoy on Lebanon, cautions that commitment by Syrian Pres Bashar al-Assad to withdraw all troops from Lebanon in next few months is contingent on formation of new government by Lebanon's leaders, task that is likely to be extremely difficult because of turbulent politics; Syria and Lebanon are to meet on April 7 to set date for withdrawal; photos (M)
news.title: Lebanon Needs to Act First For Syria to Exit, Envoy Says
Attacks kill 3 in Iraq over weekend

news.abstract: Colony of monarch butterflies that arrived in Contepec, Mexico, in November was tiny and retreated up mountains as far as possible from lower slopes where loggers have thinned or destroyed forest butterflies depend on; number arriving this winter was smallest since Mexico and World Wildlife Fund began keeping records in 1970's, down three-quarters from winter before; biologists and nature lovers blame logging in Mexico and herbicides in US for diminished numbers; photos; map (M)
news.title: Chain Saw Thins Flocks of Migrants on Gold Wings

news.abstract: Kyrgyzstan holds most fractious elections in its post-Soviet history, marked by protests and accusations of fraud; reports of vote buying and efforts to intimidate press in first round of elections for Parliament resulted in public anger; critics of Pres Askar Akayev hoped that his handpicked successor might be defeated in presidential election coming in fall; Kumanbek Bakiyev is considered most likely to defeat Akayev or designated successor; map (M)
news.title: Cries of Fraud Give Election in Kyrgyzstan Aura of Ukraine

news.abstract: Four employees of ENAV, air traffic control company for 39 Italian airports, are sentenced to up to four years in prison for manslaughter stemming from 2001 Linate airport collision that killed 118 people (S)

news.abstract: Pentagon auditors find that excess billing for postwar fuel imports to Iraq by Halliburton Co totaled more than $108 million; report was completed last fall, but has never been officially released to public or to Congress; Rep Henry A Waxman wants stronger effort to reclaim money from Halliburton; photo (M)

news.abstract: Consumer electronics introduce new ways of thinking into North Korea, perhaps corroding steely controls on ideology and information that have kept Kim family in power for almost 60 years; defectors from North Korea say that construction of cellular relay stations last fall along Chinese side of border allows some North Koreans in border towns to use prepaid Chinese cellphones to call relatives and reporters in South Korea; after DVD players swept northern China two years ago, entrepreneurs collected castoff videocassette recorders and peddled them to North Korea; tapes of South Korean soap operas are popular; photo (M)
news.title: How Electronics Are Penetrating North Korea's Isolation
Bush confidante to work on improving U.S. image
School ban on scarves wins praise

news.abstract: More than 40 heads of state and cabinet ministers, many from Europe, gather in Jerusalem for opening of new Holocaust museum at Yad Vashem; exhibits try to put human face on unimaginable horror, telling story of six million Jewish dead, names of half still unknown, through personal diaries, images and testimonies; photo; Prime Min Ariel Sharon, UN Sec Gen Kofi Annan and others speak; Mayor Michael Bloomberg leads US delegation (M)
news.title: New Museum, Putting a Human Face on the Holocaust, Opens in Israel
Handover of West Bank town of Jericho begins

news.abstract: Iraqi investigators trying to find kidnappers of Italian journalist Giuliana Sgrena are stymied by lack of cooperation from Italian intelligence services that won her release by negotiating with abductors; police official Jabbar Anwar warns kidnappings by criminal ring will continue, especially if ransom is paid, as reported in Italian media; suspicious circumstances surrounding Sgrena seizure recounted; photo (M)
news.title: Iraqis Say Italians Aren't Cooperating in Kidnapping Investigation

news.abstract: European Union postpones membership talks with Croatia; holds that Croatia is being uncooperative with United Nations war crimes tribunal since it has not captured and turned over Ante Gotovina, former Croatian general indicted by tribunal (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Europeans Halt Croatia Entry Talks
U.S. Envoy Leaves Iraq, Conceding 'Job Is Far From Done'

news.abstract: Israeli troops transfer security control to Palestinians in Jericho, West Bank town that has been nearly free of violence in recent years; move is largely symbolic but points to prospect of Israeli pullback from four other West Bank towns that Israel agreed in principle to do after truce with Palestinians was announced five weeks ago; photo; map (M)
news.title: Palestinians Gain Security Control of Jericho
World Briefings
Manila fears attack after prison toll

news.abstract: Meeting in Nairobi, Kenya, of members of Somalia's exiled Parliament ends up in brawl over makeup of peacekeeping force; one member of Parliament is seriously injured (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Africa: Somalia: Lawmakers Brawl Over Peacekeepers
Indonesia to proceed with pollution case against U.S. company

news.abstract: Barbers in Iraq live in fear of militant Islamists who are killing those who shave men's beards or do Western-style haircuts; as many as 12 barbers have been killed; many other barbers have received threats; killings and threats are not first efforts in Iraq to enforce Taliban-style religious rule; in Falluja, armed mujahedeen ran Islamic police state for months before American invasion, and in southern Iraq, Shiite militants attacked liquor stores and sometimes killed those who ignored their threats; killings and threats in Baghdad are concentrated in Doura, working-class neighborhood that has seen so much violence that police say there is little they can do to protect barbers; photos (M)
news.title: A Haircut in Iraq Can Be the Death of the Barber
Cease-fire extendedin Mideast

news.abstract: Former employee of Halliburton subsidiary Kellogg Brown & Root, Jeff Alex Mazon, is indicted along with Kuwaiti businessman, charged with defrauding United States of more than $3.5 million in subcontract to supply fuel tankers for military operations in Iraq; Mazon allegedly received bribe from Kuwaiti, Ali Hajazi, for helping his firm reap $5.5 million from contract that should have cost $2 million; Mazon has been arrested while Hijazi has not been apprehended; Halliburton claims it discovered evidence of crime and notified Justice Dept (M)
news.title: Ex-Halliburton Man Charged With Defrauding U.S. of $3.5 Million

news.abstract: Last of three articles in series China's Reach notes that China's appetite for hydroelectric power and its thrust into Southeast Asia in search of trade are changing the character of Mekong River, not only in China, but also for five nations and 60 million rural people downstream; China has built two dams, and plans to build six more along upper Mekong; conservationists say water levels and temperatures have fluctuated widely, threatening river environment and disrupting livelihoods of fishermen and others who depend on $2 billion annual catch of migratory fish; changes to river that China has already made are quickly causing way of life to recede in Myanmar, Thailand, Laos, Cambodia and Vietnam; map; photos (M)
news.title: In Life on the Mekong, China's Dams Dominate
Seeking the roots of ill health
Mercy killing of infants: A doctor explains

news.abstract: Special parliamentary committee recommends that Bobby Fischer, US chess grandmaster, be given Icelandic citizenship; Fischer has been in custody in Japan fighting deportation to US, where he is wanted for violating economic sanctions against former Yugoslavia by traveling there to play chess in 1992 (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Iceland: Citizenship Close For Bobby Fischer
India scoop: For viewers or voyeurs?

news.abstract: Senior Bush administration officials, having concluded that any American effort to mediate would likely backfire, avoid direct intervention to break deadlock among Sunni, Shiite and Kurdish factions who are still trying to form government six weeks after national elections; United States resists call from Kurds, Shiites and some Arab neighbors of Iraq to play facilitating role; Kurdish dispute with Shiites tends to overshadow parallel problem of bringing Sunnis into government (M)
news.title: U.S. Avoids Role of Mediator as Iraqis Remain Deadlocked
Putin Makes Good-Will Visit to Ukraine President

news.abstract: Humphrey Spender, prominent English artist known for his photographs documenting lives of ordinary Britons during Depression, dies at age 94; photo (M)
news.title: Humphrey Spender, Lens to British Poor, Dies at 94
Arabs to Rebuild Palestinian Homes
Pope Misses Palm Sunday Services for First Time

news.abstract: One person is killed and 735 others injured after southern Japan earthquake; 3,000 people take refuge in local gymnasiums; Genkaijima is hardest hit with most homes being damaged or destroyed (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Japan: 3,000 Seek Refuge After Quake

news.abstract: Iceland's Parliament votes to grant citizenship to American chess star Bobby Fischer; supporters say this will lay groundwork for his release from Japanese prison where he has been held since last summer, fighting deportation to United States; he has been in legal limbo since 1992 when, US says, he violated sanctions against Yugoslavia by accepting $3.3 million fee to play exhibition match there; in Iceland, where he defeated Russian world champion Boris Spassky in 1972 match in Reykjavik, he is seen as national hero (M)
news.title: Iceland Granting Citizenship to Bobby Fischer, Held in Japan
U.S. Catholic bishops taking on death penalty
High court won't rule in terror suspect case
Qaeda suspects admit plans to attack Western targets

news.title: World Briefing | Africa: Nigeria: High-Level Bribery Scandal
Mall bomb brings Lebanon closer to chaos

news.abstract: Amb Constance Morella, speaking for Energy Sec Samuel Bodman, affirms United States's strong support for nuclear energy, speech, Paris, to conference on nuclear energy; cites Pres Bush's call to resume building nuclear plants in US; warns civilian nuclear power must not be diverted to arms programs; Iranian nuclear official Mohammad Saeidi also strongly backs nuclear energy; reaffirms that Iran will develop full-scale nuclear program and not abandon its right to enrich uranium, never mentioning its temporary freeze on enrichment efforts and talks with France, Britain and Germany on permanent freeze (M)
news.title: Nuclear Power Is Good: U.S. and Iran Have No Argument There
Egypt charges opposition chief with forgery

news.abstract: Chihuahua, Mexico, judge finds Sergio Andrade, former manager and husband of singer Gloria Trevi, guilty of rape, kidnapping and corruption of minor girl and sentences him to more than seven years in prison; Andrade has already served five years since his arrest in Brazil along with Trevi; all charges were dropped against Trevi last year (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Americas: Mexico: Singer's Ex-Manager Guilty Of Rape
Swedes are soft on terrorism, Russians say

news.abstract: Health official urge travelers to avoid Angola's Uige Province after World Health Organization identifies Marburg virus, close relative of Ebola, as source of epidemic that has killed at least 95 Angolans since Oct; virus, previously identified in Uganda, Kenya and Congo, is new to Angola; United Nations officials suspend repatriation program under which tens of thousands of refugees from Angola's 21-year civil war have returned from Congo through Uige as evidence of disease spreads; Angola has begun public awareness drive stressing need for cleanliness (M)
news.title: Virus New to Angola Kills 95; Travelers Told to Avoid North
Best-selling author's life in the fishbowl

news.abstract: Arab leaders end poorly attended two-day Arab League summit conference, Algiers, with little to show for it; critics complain that resolutions passed are of comparatively little significance; leaders give little mention to Arab political reform and divisions, even though visitors like Spain's Prime Min Jose Luis Rodriguez Zapatero, French Min Michel Barnier and United Nations Sec Gen Kofi Annan prod them to discuss political reforms; use conference as forum for personal squabbles (M)
news.title: Conference of Arab Leaders Yields Little of Significance

news.abstract: Spanish police officials announce arrest of 27 people in connection with largest counterfeiting effort to be discovered in Spain since 2002 introduction of Euro; seized 2.5 million counterfeit euros during arrests (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Spain: Police Break Up Fake Euro Ring
President resigns in Kyrgyzstan
North American nations unite to compete with Asia on trade

news.abstract: Security Council unanimously passes resolution introduced by United States that would establish 10,000-member peacekeeping force for Sudan to reinforce peace agreement in south of country and to lend assistance in conflicted Darfur region in west; passage occurs after France postpones consideration of resolution that would refer war crime cases from Sudan to International Criminal Court, move seen as challenge to US and likely to provoke American veto; council members disagree over placing sanctions on Sudan, and on which court should try perpetrators of atrocities in light of American objections to international court (M)
news.title: 10,000 Peacekeepers to Be Sent to Sudan, U.N. Council Decides

news.abstract: Report on sexual abuse by United Nations peacekeepers in Congo recommends that offending soldiers and their commanders be punished by their home countries, that payments made to them be recovered and put into fund for victims and that UN make compliance with these measures condition for talking part in its missions; Secretary General Kofi Annan commissioned report after evidence emerged that blue helmeted peacekeepers and civilian staff members had sex with women and girls in Congo in exchange for food and money. and in some instances raped them; report also recommends that assistance be provided for 'peacekeeper babies' left behind when troops rotate back to their own countries; report was prepared by Prince Zeid Raad al Hussein, Jordan's ambassador to UN who is former military officer and civilian peacekeeper (M)
news.title: Report Calls for Punishing Peacekeepers in Sex Abuse

news.abstract: Toughly worded United Nations report into assassination of former Lebanese prime minister Rafik Hariri concludes that heavy-handed Syrian interference in Lebanese affairs created polarizing tensions that led to his death and that deeply flawed local investigation obstructed efforts to find his killers; report, by Patrick Fitzgerald, deputy police commissioner of Ireland, calls for investigation by independent commission as only way of uncovering truth behind Harari's killing; Secretary General Kofi Annan endorses call for international investigation; Fitzgerald's report notes that Lebanese security services ignored threats on Hariri's life, and that his security detail was cut to 8 people from 40 after he left office; photo (M)
news.title: U.N. Cites Syria as Factor in Lebanese Assassination
Two U.S. Soldiers, Marine Killed in Iraq
Parents press appeal as denials continue

news.abstract: Some signs of life are returning to Falluja four months after US bombs and guns pounded much of Iraqi city into ruins; about third of city's 250,000 residents have trickled back since early Jan; safety has come at high price, and high security has stunted renascent economy and reconstruction effort; map; photos (M)
news.title: Vital Signs of a Ruined Falluja Grow Stronger

news.abstract: US will sell F-16 jet fighters to Pakistan in deal that State Dept says will improve regional security; size of arms sale has not been decided, but Pakistan is seeking about two dozen planes; Pres Bush telephones Prime Min Manmohan Singh of India to inform him of decision; clears way for India to discuss its own purchase of combat aircraft; Singh says arms sale will undermine regional security (M)
news.title: INDIA IS CRITICAL
U.S. agrees to sell F-16 jet fighters to Pakistan
Pope Makes Appearance but Is Unable to Speak

news.abstract: Car bomb explodes in predominantly Christian Sid al Bushriya neighborhood in eastern Beirut on eve of Easter, wounding at least five people and destroying two factories in third attack on a Christian neighborhood in week; Lebanon's Christians are overwhelmingly opposed to Syria's military occupation, and many Lebanese drawn to site of bombing say they suspect Syrian involvement; photo (M)
news.title: Bomb in Christian Area of Beirut Wounds 5

news.abstract: James Callaghan, elder statesman of British Labor Party whose three years as prime minister were marked by infamous 'Winter of Discontent' and tumultuous battles with labor unions, dies at age 92; photo (M)
news.title: Lord Callaghan, British Prime Minister for 3 Tumultuous Years, Is Dead at 92

news.abstract: People of Buyat Bay region on island of Sulawesi in Indonesia are divided on cause of mysterious lumps, skin rashes, dizziness and other ailments afflicting them; some blame pollution from nearby goldmine operated by Denver-based Newmont Mining Corp and demand government relocate them; government recently announced $117 million suit against Newmont, and six Newmont executives, including two Americans, face criminal charges; environmental groups and Newmont mobilize opposing camps i n Buyat Bay, deepening animosity; photos, map (L)
news.title: Cause of Mystery Ills Splits Indonesian Fishing Village

news.abstract: American soldiers guarding sprawling southern detention center of Camp Bucca in Iraq discover largest tunnel so far found at a detention center, 12 to 16 feet underground and running 600 feet to exterior of camp; tunnel was apparently discovered before any detainees had chance to use it; it is unclear how many of camp's 6,049 detainees worked on tunnel; detainees rioted on January 31; guards began searching for escape passages after smaller tunnel was found last week; pho to (M)
news.title: U.S. Soldiers Discover Tunnel at Detention Camp
